The assignments on $x\in\mathfrak g$

$$\Delta(x)=\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)\otimes1+1\otimes\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x),\qquad \varepsilon(x)=0,\qquad S(x)=-\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)$$

extend to the standard cocommutative Hopf-algebra structure on
$U(\mathfrak g)$. The first two assignments are Lie maps into the commutator
algebras of $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g)$ and $k$, so enveloping
universality extends them to algebra maps. Interpreting the last assignment as
a Lie map into $U(\mathfrak g)^{\mathrm{op}}$ extends it to an algebra map into
the opposite algebra, equivalently an anti-algebra map $S$.

Coassociativity, cocommutativity, and the counit identities follow because the
corresponding algebra maps agree on every generator. For the antipode, write
$\Delta(a)=\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}$. Both convolution identities hold on
$1$ and on every generator, since multiplying
$-x\otimes1+1\otimes x$ gives zero. If they hold for $a$ and $b$, then

$$\sum S(a_{(1)}b_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\sum S(b_{(1)})S(a_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1,$$

and similarly

$$\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(a_{(2)}b_{(2)})=\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(b_{(2)})S(a_{(2)})=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1.$$

Induction on word length and linearity therefore prove both antipode
identities on all of $U(\mathfrak g)$.

This remark is non-load-bearing: no later item on this page depends on these
Hopf formulas.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, $S=S(\mathfrak g)$ the symmetric algebra of the adjoint
representation, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$ its invariants, $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ the
center of the enveloping algebra, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ be a Kostant
harmonic subspace, so that multiplication is an isomorphism
$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\to S$ of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules with $R$
acting trivially ([[thm-kostant-harmonic-decomposition-of-the-symmetric-algebra]]).

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ with zero-weight space
$E_0$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)$ is a free graded
$R$-module of rank $\dim E_0$, and the module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is a free $Z$-module of
rank $\dim E_0$; with the filtered lifting $U(\mathfrak g)=Z\cdot\operatorname{sym}(\mathcal H)$
of [[thm-enveloping-algebra-is-free-over-its-center]] these freenesses are
compatible with the natural quotient maps. More precisely,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\cong R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))\cong Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),$$
where $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H)$ is a finite-dimensional
graded vector space of dimension $\dim E_0$; consequently every central
reduction has adjoint $E$-multiplicity $\dim E_0$, and the natural map
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\otimes_R S/(R_+S)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S/(R_+S))$
is an isomorphism onto a space of dimension $\dim E_0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$,
and let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be homogeneous basic generators of $S(\mathfrak g)^{\mathfrak g}$
of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl
invariants ([[thm-symmetric-invariants-restrict-to-weyl-invariants]],
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]). Put
$$A=S(\mathfrak g)/(p_1,\dots,p_r).$$ Then $A$ is a reduced integral domain of
dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-r=2|\Phi^+|$, with Hilbert series
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(A,t)=\prod_{i=1}^r\frac{1-t^{d_i}}{(1-t)^{\dim\mathfrak g}},$$
and for every central character $\chi:Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\mathbb C$ the PBW
associated graded of $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ is canonically
isomorphic to $A$.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module of highest weight $\lambda$. Then the quadratic Casimir element acts on $M$ by the scalar

$$ (\lambda,\lambda+2\rho), $$

where the pairing on $\mathfrak h^*$ is induced by the Killing form and $\rho$ is the Weyl vector from [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]].

derivations.claim: If $\mathfrak g=0$ then $U(\mathfrak g)=\mathbb C$, $M(\mu)=\mathbb C$ and everything is immediate; assume $\mathfrak g\neq0$, so $N=\dim\mathfrak n^->0$. By [F2] the Verma module $M(\mu)$ has finite length, so it contains a simple submodule; by [F2] every simple object is some $L(\eta)$ and the universal map $M(\eta)\to L(\eta)\hookrightarrow M(\mu)$ is injective; hence $M(\mu)$ contains $M(\eta)$ for a highest weight $\eta$. Writing $M(\mu)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ by [F1], the submodule generated by the singular vector $p\,v_\mu$ is $U(\mathfrak n^-)p$: its embedding is right multiplication $u\mapsto up$ by a nonzero element $p\in U(\mathfrak n^-)$.

Growth: the PBW filtration of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ has $\dim F_nU(\mathfrak n^-)$ asymptotic to $n^N/N!$, while the quotient $U(\mathfrak n^-)/U(\mathfrak n^-)p$ has associated graded $S(\mathfrak n^-)/(\bar p)$ for the nonzero leading form $\bar p$ of $p$, so its Hilbert series is of the form $(1-t^d)/(1-t)^N$ and $\dim(U(\mathfrak n^-)/U(\mathfrak n^-)p)_{\le n}=O(n^{N-1})$; the same bound therefore holds for $M(\mu)/M(\eta)$ and, after tensoring by the finite-dimensional $E$, for $E\otimes(M(\mu)/M(\eta))$, because $\dim(E\otimes X)_{\le n}\le(\dim E)\dim X_{\le n}$.

The diagonal $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-action makes $E\otimes M(\mu)$ a free $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module of rank $\dim E$, by [F5] applied to the identification $M(\mu)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ of [F1]. In particular every nonzero vector $x$ of $E\otimes M(\mu)$ generates a copy $U(\mathfrak n^-)x$ of the domain $U(\mathfrak n^-)$, of growth $n^N$.

The Hom space as a kernel: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))$ is the space of $\mathfrak n^+$-invariants in the weight-$\mu$ space $(E\otimes M(\mu))_\mu$, i.e. the kernel of the finitely many raising maps $e_i:(E\otimes M(\mu))_\mu	o(E\otimes M(\mu))_{\mu+\alpha_i}$. This weight space has $\mu$-independent dimension $\sum_
u\dim E_
u\cdot\dim U(\mathfrak n^-)_
u$, and the matrices of the raising maps on fixed PBW bases have entries polynomial in $\mu$ by [F1].

Simple-Verma case: if $M(\mu)=L(\mu)$ is simple, then $D\,M(\mu)=M(\mu)$ by [F4] and $M(\mu)=
abla(\mu)$, and the tensor-hom adjunction plus [F4] give $$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E^{*}\otimes M(\mu),M(\mu)),$$ which is the multiplicity of $\Delta(\mu)$ in the standard flag of $E^{*}\otimes M(\mu)$, namely $\dim E^{*}_0=\dim E_0$: by [F4] the flag factors are the $\Delta(\mu+
u)$ with multiplicity $\dim E^{*}_
u$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta(\lambda),
abla(\mu))=\mathbb C\delta_{\lambda\mu}$ while $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ vanishes.

Lower bound for all $\mu$: the dimension of the kernel of step 1.4 is $\dim(E\otimes M(\mu))_\mu$ minus the rank of the polynomial matrix there; the rank at any $\mu$ is at most the maximal rank, attained on the dense open set where $M(\mu)$ is simple, where it equals the value computed in step 1.5; hence $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))\ge\dim E_0$ for every $\mu$.

Upper bound: the restriction map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\eta),E\otimes M(\eta))$$ is injective. First, every $\varphi$ takes $M(\eta)$ into $E\otimes M(\eta)$: otherwise the composition with the projection $E\otimes(M(\mu)/M(\eta))$ would embed the simple $M(\eta)$, a copy of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ of growth $n^N$ by step 1.1, into the module of growth $O(n^{N-1})$ from step 1.2, impossible. Second, if $\varphi\neq0$ killed $M(\eta)$, it would factor through $M(\mu)/M(\eta)$ and its nonzero image would contain, by step 1.3, a copy of the domain $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ of growth $n^N$, again contradicting step 1.2.

Action injectivity setup: let $v$ be the highest vector of the simple Verma $M(\eta)\subseteq M(\mu)$ found in step 1.1 and pair $U(\mathfrak n^+)_ eta$ with $U(\mathfrak n^-)_{ eta}$ by the Shapovalov form of $M(\eta)$, perfect in each weight by [F3]. For $0
eq x=\sum_ eta x_ eta$ in $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)$, choose a minimal $ eta$ with $x_ eta=\sum_i b_i\otimes a_i
eq0$ and a dual PBW vector $a_j^{*}\in U(\mathfrak n^-)_{ eta}$ with $\langle a_i,a_j^{*}angle=\delta_{ij}$; acting on $a_j^{*}v$ all components of weight other than $ eta$ vanish by minimality and highest-weight support, and the surviving component is $b_jv$ for the index $j$ with $b_j
eq0$. Hence the composite $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)	o U(\mathfrak g)	o\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)$ is injective; its image has cumulative PBW growth bounded below by a positive multiple of $n^{2N}$.

Combining steps 1.5, 2.1 and 2.2, $$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$$ for every highest weight $\mu$ and every finite-dimensional $E$; the same computation with $E$ replaced by its dual identifies the adjoint isotypic multiplicity in $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules with $\dim E_0$, by the freeness statement of [F6].

Suppose the action had nonzero kernel $K$ in $U_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Then the associated graded $\operatorname{gr}(K)$ is a nonzero graded ideal of the domain $A$ of [F6], so it contains $Af$ for a nonzero homogeneous $f$; multiplication by $f$ is injective and the complete-intersection Hilbert series of $A$ gives $\dim(A/Af)_{\le n}=O(n^{2N-1})$. Consequently the image of $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)$ in $U_\chi$ has cumulative growth $O(n^{2N-1})$, contradicting the lower bound of step 2.3. Hence the action $U_\chi\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)$ is injective.

Surjectivity onto the locally finite part: the map of step 3.2 is $\mathfrak g$-equivariant for the adjoint actions, so it maps the $E$-isotypic component to the $E$-isotypic component for every finite-dimensional simple $E$. The source $E$-isotypic multiplicity is $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U_\chi)=\dim E_0$ by [F6], and the target multiplicity is $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E\otimes M(\mu),M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E^{*}\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$ by step 3.1. An injective linear map between spaces of equal finite dimension is an isomorphism, so the action is an isomorphism onto each isotypic component, hence onto the locally finite part.

Since the kernel of $U(\mathfrak g)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)$ and the image of $U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$ lies in that kernel, steps 3.2 and 4.1 give both the algebra isomorphism and $\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$; the multiplicity statement is step 3.1 read through the isomorphism. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the published category-$\mathcal O$ and invariant-theory suppliers.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block and
translation theory ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]).

Fix the dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ of a regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]) and an
integral weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and
$\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$ for a reflection
$s=s_\alpha$; this is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall translation
data, the published
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] being stated with
antidominant representatives, and the dominant standard counts below are
proved through the norm-distance and extremal-weight bounds
([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]],
[[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) rather than
by applying that datum literally. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant element of
the linear Weyl orbit of $\mu-\lambda$ and let
$E=L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\nu$, so
that $\mu-\lambda$ is an extremal weight of $E$; write
$E^{*}=L(-w_0\nu)$ for its dual
([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).

With $\chi_\lambda,\chi_\mu$ the generalized central characters and
$\operatorname{pr}$ the exact central projections of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], define the **onto-wall** and
**out-of-wall** translations
$$T_{\mathrm{on}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(E\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ(E^{*}\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}},$$
and the **wall-crossing functor**
$$\theta_s:=T_{\mathrm{out}}\circ T_{\mathrm{on}}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** Both translations are exact, and $T_{\mathrm{out}}$ is
both a left and a right adjoint of $T_{\mathrm{on}}$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]); hence
$\theta_s$ is exact and, as a composite of restriction-of-scalars and central
block projection applied to tensoring by $E^{*}\otimes E$, it is a natural
direct summand of the endofunctor
$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ((E^{*}\otimes E)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}$,
so it is a projective functor on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]. On
standard objects the dominant-chamber counts are
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and the
two-factor flag $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w\cdot s\cdot\lambda)]$ for
$T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, by
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]] applied after
transporting the wall datum to its antidominant representative.

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair
$(\theta_s,\eta,\varepsilon)$ is determined by the choice of the
biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct
$\theta_s$ or to generate objects.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$(\lambda,\mu,\alpha)$ be a single-wall translation datum with translating
weight $\nu$, wall reflection $s=s_\alpha$, and $E=L(\nu)$, and let
$T_\lambda^\mu$ and $T_\mu^\lambda$ be the translation functors of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Then:

1. $T_\lambda^\mu\Delta(w\mathbin\cdot\lambda)\cong
   \Delta(w\mathbin\cdot\mu)$ for every $w\in W$;
2. $T_\mu^\lambda\Delta(w\mathbin\cdot\mu)$ has a finite Verma flag with
   exactly two factors, $\Delta(w\mathbin\cdot\lambda)$ and
   $\Delta(w\mathbin\cdot(s\mathbin\cdot\lambda))
   =\Delta(w s\mathbin\cdot\lambda)$, each occurring with multiplicity one; in
   particular its class in the Grothendieck group is
   $[\Delta(w\mathbin\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w s\mathbin\cdot\lambda)]$.

transporting the wall datum to its antidominant representative.

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair

biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $X\in\mathcal O$
admits two finite Verma flags with corresponding multiplicities
$m_\mu$ and $m'_\mu$
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]), then $m_\mu=m'_\mu$ for every
weight $\mu$. Hence the multiplicity $(X:\Delta(\mu))$ of
[[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] is well defined.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $X=X_1\oplus X_2$
is a direct sum decomposition in $\mathcal O$ and $X$ is Verma-filtered
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]), then both $X_1$ and $X_2$ are
Verma-filtered.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module with weight
multiplicities $\dim E_\eta$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). For every
weight $\mu$, the object $E\otimes\Delta(\mu)$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]) whose factors are $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$,
the factor $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$ occurring $\dim E_\eta$ times; the factors can be
ordered so that a real-linear height $\ell$ with $\ell(\alpha_i)=1$ is nonincreasing.

Consequently, if $X\in\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(\nu))$, then $E\otimes X$ has a finite Verma flag and
$$(E\otimes X:\Delta(\mu))=\sum_\eta\dim E_\eta\,(X:\Delta(\mu-\eta)).$$

derivations.claim: $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ by the first clause of [F1], hence it has the two-factor finite Verma flag of the second clause of [F1] with factors $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each once; its class in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ is $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)]$ by [F2].

Let $X$ be Verma-filtered with finite flag $0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$ and factors $\Delta(v_i\cdot\lambda)$. Exactness of $\theta_s$ by [F2] makes $0=\theta_sX_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\theta_sX_n=\theta_sX$ an increasing chain of subobjects, and each quotient $\theta_sX_i/\theta_sX_{i-1}\cong\theta_s(X_i/X_{i-1})\cong\theta_s\Delta(v_i\cdot\lambda)$ carries the two-factor flag of step 1.1; concatenating these two-step flags through the chain yields a finite Verma flag of $\theta_sX$ with factor multiplicities $(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$, where the independence of the flag [F2] makes the count well defined.

Summing the classes along the flag of step 2.1 gives $[\theta_sX]=\sum_i([\Delta(v_i\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(v_is\cdot\lambda)])=[X]+\sum_i[\Delta(v_is\cdot\lambda)]$, which is the stated formula $(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$; no splitting of the two-step extensions is used, and the claim extends to direct summands of $\theta_sX$ whenever they are Verma-filtered, by [F3].

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of
the Cartan subalgebra of [[def-bgg-category-o]], graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$
as fixed on this page ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]],
[[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]). Let
$\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$
by
$$x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak h),\qquad x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak n^+),$$
where $xs$ denotes the action on $S$ through
$\mathfrak b\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak h$ by weight. Put
$$M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda),$$
a module over $\mathfrak g\otimes S$: the left $\mathfrak g$-action is induced,
and $S$ acts on the right by multiplication on the last factor, which commutes
with $\mathfrak g$. Specializing at a closed point $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$ gives
$$M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon),$$
the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]; this is the universal family of
Verma modules with deformation parameter $\epsilon$.

**The family.** For a localization $T$ of $S$ put
$M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$, and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the
full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of
a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak g$-modules $E$. Write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for
$R=S_{(0)}$, the localization of $S$ at the origin of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment
$T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} T$. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents of highest weights
$\lambda+\nu+\epsilon$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors, and they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and generically the Verma constituents
have pairwise distinct central characters except for repeated identical
labels, as read off the Shapovalov determinant
([[thm-shapovalov-determinant-formula]]).

**Selected components.** For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] and a
dot-dominant integral target $\nu$, so that $\nu+\rho$ lies in the closed
positive chamber, denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ the component of
$\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber at the origin lies in the selected
target block $\mathcal O_\nu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Finite Verma flags of the
deformed tensor products and pairwise-unit resultants of their
central-character polynomials define this component by actual central
idempotents over $R$, obtained from the Chinese remainder theorem applied in
$R[X]$ to a central element separating the finitely many special central
characters. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor
family; thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are
distinguished.

**Weight structure.** Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an
$\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition whose weight spaces are locally free of
finite rank over $T$, as follows from the PBW model of Verma modules and the
flatness of the localization
([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, $S=S(\mathfrak g)$ the symmetric algebra of the adjoint
representation, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$ its invariants, $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ the
center of the enveloping algebra, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ be a Kostant
harmonic subspace, so that multiplication is an isomorphism
$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\to S$ of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules with $R$
acting trivially ([[thm-kostant-harmonic-decomposition-of-the-symmetric-algebra]]).

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ with zero-weight space
$E_0$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)$ is a free graded
$R$-module of rank $\dim E_0$, and the module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is a free $Z$-module of
rank $\dim E_0$; with the filtered lifting $U(\mathfrak g)=Z\cdot\operatorname{sym}(\mathcal H)$
of [[thm-enveloping-algebra-is-free-over-its-center]] these freenesses are
compatible with the natural quotient maps. More precisely,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\cong R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))\cong Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),$$
where $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H)$ is a finite-dimensional
graded vector space of dimension $\dim E_0$; consequently every central
reduction has adjoint $E$-multiplicity $\dim E_0$, and the natural map
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\otimes_R S/(R_+S)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S/(R_+S))$
is an isomorphism onto a space of dimension $\dim E_0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g)$ is a free left, hence also right, module over its center $Z(U(\mathfrak g))$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, set $S=S(\mathfrak g)$, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$, and let $\mathcal H$ be its Kostant harmonic subspace. Multiplication is an isomorphism
$$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S$$
of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules, where $R$ carries the trivial action. The assertion includes $\mathfrak g=0$.

Orbit sums indexed by the distinct $W$-orbits in $P$ form a complex vector-space basis of $\mathbb C[P]^W$. Equivalently they are indexed by dominant integral weights, with exactly one per orbit, including weights on chamber walls. Every invariant has finite support in this basis.

For each dominant $\lambda$, the set of dominant $\mu\le\lambda$ is finite. In fact every such $\mu$ satisfies $\|\mu\|\le\|\lambda\|$ for the specified invariant Euclidean norm. All assertions are choice-free.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Fix finite-dimensional $E,F$ and consider the relative $\lambda$-weight space $W_T:=(E\otimes F^{*}\otimes M_T(\lambda))_{\lambda}$; by [F1] it is a finite free $T$-module, and the $\mathfrak n^+$-invariance equations $e_iw=0$ are given by a matrix $A$ with entries in $T$ acting on $W_T$. Tensor-hom adjunction identifies the kernel of $A$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$: maps are determined by the image of the highest-weight generator and land in the $\lambda$-weight space.

The rank $s$ of $A$ is constant on closed fibers: by [F2] the kernel of $A\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)$ has dimension $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$ for every closed point $\epsilon$ (the fiber of $E\otimes F^{*}\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ at $\epsilon$ is $E\otimes F^{*}\otimes M(\lambda+\epsilon)$), and the domain $W_T\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)$ has constant dimension, so the rank is constant; hence every $(s+1)$-minor of $A$ vanishes and the $s$-minors have no common zero on $\operatorname{Spec}T$, so they generate the unit ideal.

Consequently, on the principal open subsets where an $s$-minor is invertible, Gaussian elimination puts $A$ into the normal form $\operatorname{diag}(I_s,0)$, and the kernel of $A$ is a finite projective $T$-module, locally free of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$; over the graded localization $T$ it is in fact free of that rank, and its formation commutes with every base change, including residue fields of nonclosed primes. This proves the rank and base-change assertions of (2) for the stated Hom spaces, and (3) for summands.

The action is an isomorphism on every isotypic component, by the same finite-matrix argument applied to the source: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is free over $Z$ of rank $\dim E_0$ by [F2], its closed-fiber maps $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi\to(\operatorname{End}M(\mu))^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}}$ are the Duflo–Joseph isomorphisms by [F2], so the image and cokernel form finite modules whose closed fibers vanish; by local Nakayama at every maximal ideal the cokernel vanishes, and the equal-rank projective kernel vanishes as well. Hence the action is an isomorphism on each isotypic component and, by local finiteness of the adjoint action, on the whole $\mathfrak g$-finite part, giving (1).

Passing from $\operatorname{Hom}$ of tensor objects to the kernel computation of step 1.1 is natural in $E,F$, so the free rank and base-change isomorphisms of (2) follow for $M,N$ ranging over finite direct sums of tensor objects and their direct summands: images of split idempotents in these Hom modules remain finite projective and locally free, preserving all base-change isomorphisms.

For (4): a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map $f:M\to N$ in $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose special fiber is an isomorphism has, on each of the finite free $R$-weight spaces, a matrix whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is invertible; by the determinant/Nakayama argument over the local ring $R$, each such matrix is invertible, so $f$ is an isomorphism. The constructions use the harmonic freeness and the Harish-Chandra identification of [F3], and the Axiom of Choice is inherited from the published suppliers.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The classes $[L(\lambda)]$, and separately the classes $[M(\lambda)]$, form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O)$. For a fixed finite central-character label set $\Lambda=W\cdot\lambda$, the transition between its standard and simple classes is unitriangular in any linear order extending $\leq$. This remains true on a downward-closed subset of that finite poset. It is not a claim about finite downward ideals of all of $\mathfrak h^*$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let
$\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection
$s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the
object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two
factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with
multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group
$$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$
Moreover $\theta_s$ is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects with finite
Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_sX$ has one with multiplicities
$(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$,
and the same formula holds in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$. The resulting flag is
not in general split; splitting is neither asserted nor used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block and
translation theory ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]).

Fix the dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ of a regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]) and an
integral weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and
$\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$ for a reflection
$s=s_\alpha$; this is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall translation
data, the published
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] being stated with
antidominant representatives, and the dominant standard counts below are
proved through the norm-distance and extremal-weight bounds
([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]],
[[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) rather than
by applying that datum literally. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant element of
the linear Weyl orbit of $\mu-\lambda$ and let
$E=L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\nu$, so
that $\mu-\lambda$ is an extremal weight of $E$; write
$E^{*}=L(-w_0\nu)$ for its dual
([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).

With $\chi_\lambda,\chi_\mu$ the generalized central characters and
$\operatorname{pr}$ the exact central projections of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], define the **onto-wall** and
**out-of-wall** translations
$$T_{\mathrm{on}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(E\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ(E^{*}\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}},$$
and the **wall-crossing functor**
$$\theta_s:=T_{\mathrm{out}}\circ T_{\mathrm{on}}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** Both translations are exact, and $T_{\mathrm{out}}$ is
both a left and a right adjoint of $T_{\mathrm{on}}$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]); hence
$\theta_s$ is exact and, as a composite of restriction-of-scalars and central
block projection applied to tensoring by $E^{*}\otimes E$, it is a natural
direct summand of the endofunctor
$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ((E^{*}\otimes E)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}$,
so it is a projective functor on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]. On
standard objects the dominant-chamber counts are
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and the
two-factor flag $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w\cdot s\cdot\lambda)]$ for
$T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, by
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]] applied after
transporting the wall datum to its antidominant representative.

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair
$(\theta_s,\eta,\varepsilon)$ is determined by the choice of the
biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct
$\theta_s$ or to generate objects.

For the geometric finite Weyl group and its simple reflections, define $u\le v$ when a reduced expression for $v$ contains a reduced expression for $u$ as an ordered subword: choose positions in increasing order, multiply their letters in that order, and require their number to be $\ell(u)$. The empty subword represents the identity.

The following proof shows this condition is independent of the reduced expression for $v$ and is equivalent to a chain $u=w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_k=v$ with $w_{j+1}=t_jw_j$, each $t_j$ a root reflection and $\ell(w_{j+1})=\ell(w_j)+1$. Thus it is a partial order, called **strong Bruhat order**. A zero-length chain is allowed. The subword and saturated-reflection-chain descriptions are proved equivalent here; neither an abstract Coxeter presentation nor weak order or inversion-set containment is being substituted.

derivations.claim: The map $c$ is a well-defined homomorphism: every object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ has a finite Verma flag, its class is the sum of the factor classes, and by [F1] the classes of the standards are a $\mathbb Z$-basis indexed by the $|W|$ elements of $W$; sending the basis element $[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]$ to $v$ therefore extends uniquely to an isomorphism of free abelian groups of rank $|W|$.

On every Verma class the formula holds: $c[\theta_s\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]=v+vs=v(1+s)=c[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]\cdot(1+s)$ by [F2], using that right multiplication by $s$ in $\mathbb Z[W]$ sends the basis element $v$ to $vs$. Since $\theta_s$ is exact by [F2] and every $X$ carries a finite Verma flag, applying $\theta_s$ to a flag and summing the factorwise classes gives $c[\theta_sX]=c[X](1+s)$ for all $X\in\mathcal O_\lambda$, and both sides are additive in $X$.

Iterate step 2.1 along the word, applying the factors in the order in which they act: the composite $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$ applies $\theta_{s_1}$ first, so $c[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(((1+s_1))(1+s_2))\cdots(1+s_k)=(1+s_1)(1+s_2)\cdots(1+s_k)$; expanding the product gives the sum over all subwords $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, $i_1<\cdots<i_r$, of their products, with the multiplicity with which each product arises. The full subword contributes $w$ once; every proper subword has strictly smaller length, and its product is $\le w$ with smaller length, hence strictly smaller than $w$ in the Bruhat order by [F3]. Reversing the order of composition multiplies the factors in the reverse order, as recorded.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]],
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie
algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: a Cartan
subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, the
Weyl group $W$ of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]], the Weyl
vector $\rho$, and the dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Write
$Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\le\lambda$ when
$\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$.

**The fixed weight.** Fix a weight $\lambda$ which is **integral**,
**dot-regular** and **dominant**: $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$
for every root $\alpha$ (so the integral Weyl group $W_\lambda$ of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is all of $W$), and
$\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$, respectively $>0$, for every
root, respectively every positive root ([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]).
The set $\Phi_\lambda$ of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is therefore
the full root system and $W_\lambda=W$.

**The block.** Regularity makes the dot-action stabilizer
$\{w\in W:w\cdot\lambda=\lambda\}$ trivial, since $w\cdot\lambda=\lambda$ forces
$\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ for every root $\alpha$ reflected by
$w$; hence the linkage class
$$C=W_\lambda\cdot\lambda=W\cdot\lambda$$
has exactly $|W|$ elements. The **regular integral block** is the full
subcategory
$$\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$$
of objects of $\mathcal O$ whose simple composition factors have labels in
$C$, as in [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is
$\{0\}$-free, abelian and extension-closed as a block, and
$K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ is the subgroup of $K_0(\mathcal O)$ of
[[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]] spanned by the classes
of objects of the block.

**Its labelled objects.** For $w\in W$ define the standard and costandard
objects and the simple object by
$$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda),\qquad \nabla(w\cdot\lambda):=D(M(w\cdot\lambda)),\qquad L(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda)/J(w\cdot\lambda),$$
where $M$ is the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]], $D$ the restricted dual
of [[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], and $J(w\cdot\lambda)$
the sum of all proper submodules, so that $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique
simple quotient of $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ by
[[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]. By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ are exactly the $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for
$w\in W$, pairwise non-isomorphic. Let $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ denote a projective
cover of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, which may be chosen inside the linkage class of
$w\cdot\lambda$ and is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); every such $P(w\cdot\lambda)$
carries a finite Verma flag
([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]],
[[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

**Triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix.** For all $v,w\in W$,
$$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\ \Longrightarrow\ v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda,\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1,$$
where the multiplicity is the composition multiplicity of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]. Indeed
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]$
by [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] and
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))\neq0$ forces
$w\cdot\lambda-v\cdot\lambda\in Q^+$ while
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))=1$ by
[[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]].

**The antidominant weight.** Let $w_0\in W$ be the longest element. Since
$\langle w_0\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle
=\langle\lambda+\rho,w_0^{-1}\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ for every positive root
$\alpha$, the antidominant Verma module $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is simple
([[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]]), so
$$\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$
and this is the unique standard object of the block that is simple: for
$w\neq w_0$ the regular weight $w\cdot\lambda$ is not antidominant, so some
positive root $\alpha$ has
$\langle w\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, and
[[thm-verma-embedding-for-an-arbitrary-positive-root]] embeds
$M(s_\alpha\cdot(w\cdot\lambda))$ as a proper submodule of
$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$. The weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ is called the
**antidominant weight** of the block and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ its
antidominant Verma module.

**Grothendieck group.** By [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]
applied to the finite label set $C=W\cdot\lambda$, both the classes
$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]$ and the classes $[L(w\cdot\lambda)]$, $w\in W$,
form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$, and the transition matrix
between them is unitriangular for any linear order of $W$ extending the order
on the dot orbit induced by $\le$.

Every statement above uses the published block, Verma, duality and
projective-cover theory named in the citations, and that theory assumes the
Axiom of Choice; the definition itself selects nothing further.

For a $\mathfrak g$-module $V$, sending a homomorphism $T:M(\lambda)\to V$
to $T(v_\lambda)$ is a bijection onto the vectors $v\in V$ of weight
$\lambda$ annihilated by $\mathfrak n^+$.  Here $M(\lambda)$ is
[[def-verma-module]].  The nonzero vectors in this target are precisely the
highest-weight vectors of weight $\lambda$ from
[[def-highest-weight-vector-and-cyclic-highest-weight-module]]; the zero vector
corresponds to the zero homomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Fix a regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], with
inclusion $\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\to\mathcal O$ and
exact projection $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$
of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], so that
$\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda=\operatorname{id}$;
the block is a direct summand of $\mathcal O$ and contains the projective
covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ of [[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]. For a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ define
the endofunctor
$$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** The functor $F_E$ is well defined and additive:
$E\otimes-$ is an exact endofunctor of $\mathcal O$ and maps $\mathcal O$ into
itself ([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is exact. Hence $F_E$ is exact as a composite of
exact functors. It preserves projective objects: if $P\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ is
projective, then $E\otimes P$ is projective in $\mathcal O$
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ preserves projectives
([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]). The identity module $E=0$
gives the zero functor, and $E=\mathbb C$ the identity functor, since the
one-dimensional trivial module acts by the identity.

**Projective functors.** A **projective functor** on
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a
direct summand of some $F_E$, $E$ finite dimensional and
$\mathfrak h$-semisimple. Write $\mathcal F_\lambda$ for the full subcategory
of the endofunctor category of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ whose objects are the
projective functors, with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms; it is
additive with the pointwise biproducts of [[def-additive-category]], and
"direct summand" means a pair of mutually inverse idempotent splittings as in
the idempotent-completion convention of that definition.

**Closure properties.** The class of projective functors is closed under
finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints:

1. $F_{E\oplus E'}\cong F_E\oplus F_{E'}$, since tensoring with a direct sum
distributes over direct sums and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is additive.
2. $F_E\circ F_{E'}\cong F_{E\otimes E'}$: inserting
$\operatorname{incl}_\lambda\circ\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ between the two
factors and using the associativity of the tensor product of finite-dimensional
modules identifies the composite with
$\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ((E\otimes E')\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda$.
3. $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$: this is
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] applied to
the two generalized central characters of the block, since
$F_{E^*}=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E^*\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda$
is the translation functor $T_{\chi_\lambda,E^*,\chi_\lambda}$ and similarly for
$F_E$.
4. A direct summand of an exact additive functor is exact, and a direct summand
of a functor preserving projective objects again preserves projective objects:
apply the splitting to the image of each object. Hence every projective functor
is exact and preserves projective objects, and the class is closed under
composition and finite direct sums.

This is the definition of Bernstein-Gelfand [BGe, Section 3.1] and of
[Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not
required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a
direct summand of one.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If a projective object
$P$ of $\mathcal O$ admits an epimorphism $P\twoheadrightarrow L$ onto a
simple object $L$, then some indecomposable direct summand of $P$ maps onto
$L$, and that summand is a projective cover of $L$ (an essential epimorphism
with projective source, [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]).
Any two projective covers of $L$ are isomorphic, although not canonically so,
and the endomorphism ring of a projective cover is local. In particular, for
every simple $L$ there is at most one isomorphism class of indecomposable
projectives with head $L$; when such a cover exists it is written $P(L)$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category in which every object has finite
length, and define an object to be **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and
every decomposition $X\cong Y\oplus Z$ has $Y=0$ or $Z=0$. Then:

1. every object of $\mathcal A$ is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
   objects;
2. the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable object is local, and for an
   endomorphism $f$ of an indecomposable object either $f$ is an isomorphism
   or $f$ is nilpotent;
3. the decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and permutation of the
   summands;
4. an indecomposable projective object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ has a unique
   maximal proper subobject $J(P)$, its quotient $P/J(P)$ is simple, and $P$
   is a projective cover of $P/J(P)$
   ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]];
   projectivity here is relative to $\mathcal A$. In a full subcategory closed
   under submodules, essentiality is the superfluous-kernel condition of the
   cited module definition; projectivity in the ambient module category is
   not asserted).

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the
regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the
assignment
$$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the
wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies
$$c\,[\theta_sX]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$.
Consequently, for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$ one has
$$c\,[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s_1)(1+s_2)\cdots(1+s_k),$$
the sum of all subexpression products with their actual multiplicities; its top
Bruhat term is $w$ once and all other terms have strictly smaller labels. With
the composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ instead, the factors are
multiplied in the reverse order.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let
$\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection
$s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the
object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two
factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with
multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group
$$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$
Moreover $\theta_s$ is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects with finite
Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_sX$ has one with multiplicities
$(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$,
and the same formula holds in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$. The resulting flag is
not in general split; splitting is neither asserted nor used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If
$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))$ is nonzero then $\mu\ge\lambda$, that is,
$\mu-\lambda\in Q^+$. Moreover $(P(\lambda):\Delta(\lambda))=1$, so exactly
one factor of every Verma flag of $P(\lambda)$ has label $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

If $[M(\lambda):L(\mu)]\ne0$, then $\mu\uparrow\lambda$.

For the simple reflections of a finite reduced crystallographic root system, word length equals inversion length: $\ell(w)=|\operatorname{Inv}(w)|$. If a root reflection $t$ satisfies $\ell(tw)<\ell(w)$, every reduced word for $w$ loses exactly one letter to give $tw$. Every nonreduced word admits deletion of two letters without changing its group element.

More precisely, for $\beta\in\Phi^+$, $\ell(s_\beta w)<\ell(w)$ if and only if $w^{-1}\beta<0$. In this case one letter can be deleted from any word for $w$ to give $s_\beta w$, although the resulting word need not be reduced. Also $\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)\pm1$, with the minus sign exactly when $w\alpha_i<0$. These are assertions for the geometric reflection group, without an assumed Coxeter presentation or exchange axiom.

For the geometric finite Weyl group and its simple reflections, define $u\le v$ when a reduced expression for $v$ contains a reduced expression for $u$ as an ordered subword: choose positions in increasing order, multiply their letters in that order, and require their number to be $\ell(u)$. The empty subword represents the identity.

The following proof shows this condition is independent of the reduced expression for $v$ and is equivalent to a chain $u=w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_k=v$ with $w_{j+1}=t_jw_j$, each $t_j$ a root reflection and $\ell(w_{j+1})=\ell(w_j)+1$. Thus it is a partial order, called **strong Bruhat order**. A zero-length chain is allowed. The subword and saturated-reflection-chain descriptions are proved equivalent here; neither an abstract Coxeter presentation nor weak order or inversion-set containment is being substituted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

For weights $\lambda,\mu$, a nonzero homomorphism $M(\mu)\to M(\lambda)$ exists if and only if $\mu\uparrow\lambda$.

derivations.claim: The object $Y:=\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)$ is projective by [F1], and the block has finite-dimensional Hom spaces and finite decompositions, so $Y\cong\bigoplus_xP(x\cdot\lambda)^{m_x}$ with nonnegative multiplicities; its standard-flag multiplicities are read from its class in [F2], and every standard factor has a label $\le w$.

No summand $P(x\cdot\lambda)$ with $x\not\le w$ occurs: the diagonal entry of the BGG matrix gives $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))=1$ by [F3], so such a summand would contribute a standard factor $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ to $Y$ with $x\not\le w$, contradicting step 1.1.

The full subexpression contributes $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ with multiplicity one to the product class, and no other summand $P(x\cdot\lambda)$ with $x\le w$, $x\neq w$ contributes to the multiplicity of $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$: $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))\neq0$ forces $w\le x$ by [F3], so with $x\le w$ it forces $x=w$. Hence $m_w=1$, and the only summand whose flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ is $P(w\cdot\lambda)$.

The remaining multiplicities $m_x$, $x<w$, are determined recursively from the product class: the coefficient of $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ in the class of $Y$ equals $m_x+\sum_{x<z}m_z(P(z\cdot\lambda):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))$, whose second term involves only strictly larger labels already determined; solving downward in the finite Bruhat order gives all $m_x$.

Every indecomposable projective is a summand of such a word: the decomposition of step 1.1 with diagonal support realizes each $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ as a summand of $\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)$ for any reduced word $w$, which is the stated generation statement.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of
the Cartan subalgebra of [[def-bgg-category-o]], graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$
as fixed on this page ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]],
[[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]). Let
$\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$
by
$$x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak h),\qquad x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak n^+),$$
where $xs$ denotes the action on $S$ through
$\mathfrak b\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak h$ by weight. Put
$$M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda),$$
a module over $\mathfrak g\otimes S$: the left $\mathfrak g$-action is induced,
and $S$ acts on the right by multiplication on the last factor, which commutes
with $\mathfrak g$. Specializing at a closed point $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$ gives
$$M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon),$$
the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]; this is the universal family of
Verma modules with deformation parameter $\epsilon$.

**The family.** For a localization $T$ of $S$ put
$M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$, and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the
full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of
a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak g$-modules $E$. Write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for
$R=S_{(0)}$, the localization of $S$ at the origin of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment
$T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} T$. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents of highest weights
$\lambda+\nu+\epsilon$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors, and they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and generically the Verma constituents
have pairwise distinct central characters except for repeated identical
labels, as read off the Shapovalov determinant
([[thm-shapovalov-determinant-formula]]).

**Selected components.** For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] and a
dot-dominant integral target $\nu$, so that $\nu+\rho$ lies in the closed
positive chamber, denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ the component of
$\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber at the origin lies in the selected
target block $\mathcal O_\nu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Finite Verma flags of the
deformed tensor products and pairwise-unit resultants of their
central-character polynomials define this component by actual central
idempotents over $R$, obtained from the Chinese remainder theorem applied in
$R[X]$ to a central element separating the finitely many special central
characters. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor
family; thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are
distinguished.

**Weight structure.** Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an
$\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition whose weight spaces are locally free of
finite rank over $T$, as follows from the PBW model of Verma modules and the
flatness of the localization
([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.

For a $\mathfrak g$-module $V$, sending a homomorphism $T:M(\lambda)\to V$
to $T(v_\lambda)$ is a bijection onto the vectors $v\in V$ of weight
$\lambda$ annihilated by $\mathfrak n^+$.  Here $M(\lambda)$ is
[[def-verma-module]].  The nonzero vectors in this target are precisely the
highest-weight vectors of weight $\lambda$ from
[[def-highest-weight-vector-and-cyclic-highest-weight-module]]; the zero vector
corresponds to the zero homomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h$ be any Cartan subalgebra in the
nilpotent self-normalizing sense, and fix a positive root system with Weyl
group $W$ and half-sum $\rho$ of its positive roots. The shifted Harish-Chandra map

$$ \operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S(\mathfrak h)^W, \qquad \operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda-\rho), $$

is an algebra isomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a chosen positive-root system and corresponding Borel, Weyl group $W$, and half-sum $\rho$ of positive roots. Let $\chi_\lambda$ and $\chi_\mu$ be the central characters obtained from highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ for this Borel. Then

$$\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu \quad \text{if and only if} \quad \mu\in W\cdot \lambda,$$

where $W\cdot \lambda:=\{w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho : w\in W\}$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

**Weight structure.** Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an
$\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition whose weight spaces are locally free of

([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

length, and define an object to be **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and

   objects;
2. the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable object is local, and for an
   endomorphism $f$ of an indecomposable object either $f$ is an isomorphism

3. the decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and permutation of the

4. an indecomposable projective object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ has a unique
   maximal proper subobject $J(P)$, its quotient $P/J(P)$ is simple, and $P$
   is a projective cover of $P/J(P)$
   ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]];
   projectivity here is relative to $\mathcal A$. In a full subcategory closed
   under submodules, essentiality is the superfluous-kernel condition of the
   cited module definition; projectivity in the ambient module category is

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I \trianglelefteq R$ satisfy $I \subseteq J(R)$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated left $R$-module. If $IM=M$, then $M=0$.

derivations.claim: For $\xi\le\lambda$, the truncated induced object $Q_R(\xi)$ of [F1] represents the weight functor $N\mapsto N^\xi$ on the truncated category: evaluating at the cyclic tensor generator shows that all excluded positive PBW monomials kill a vector of weight $\xi$, so $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_R(\xi),N)\cong N^\xi$. Consequently $Q_R(\xi)$ is projective, and for finite sums and direct summands this Hom functor still commutes with arbitrary algebra base change, being the image of a split weight-space idempotent.

Central components are isolated by actual central projectors: by [F2] the Chinese remainder construction over $R[X]$ produces idempotents cutting out the selected component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ from the full tensor family, without any completion. Direct summands of the resulting finite projectives are again deformed Verma-filtered by [F3].

Induct over the finite dot orbit downward from the dominant weight. The selected $Q_R(\lambda)$ has residue fiber containing $P(\lambda)$ once and only projectives $P(\eta)$ with $\eta>\lambda$ besides; subtracting the higher terms successively with the unitriangular BGG matrix over the residue field ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) leaves a projective whose residue fiber is exactly $P(\lambda)$, giving $P_R(\lambda)$. Replacing $Q_R(\xi)$ by the corresponding truncated object at a general $\xi$ and repeating the same subtraction along the orbit yields $P_R(\xi)$ with residue fiber $P(\xi)$ for every orbit element; the construction is unique up to isomorphism because a projective with a given residue decompositions and no higher terms is determined by its class.

Wall-crossing compositions over $R$ lift the covering statement of [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]: the projected tensor word over $R$ has a finite deformed Verma flag whose multiplicities specialize to those at the origin, and its residue-fiber decomposition into the $P(x)$ lifts through the finite projective lifting of step 2.2, so every indecomposable of the selected component is one of the $P_R(x,\lambda)$. Each lift has the same flag multiplicities as its closed fiber.

Base change: for a map $R\to R'$ of deformation algebras, the representing property of step 1.1 gives the displayed isomorphism for finite sums of the $Q_R(\xi)$ and hence, by taking images of split idempotents, for all finite projectives and finite Verma-filtered targets; the module is finite free over the local ring $R$ by step 1.1.

A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such objects with isomorphic residue fiber acts invertibly on each finite free weight space modulo the maximal ideal; by [F4] it is invertible on each weight space, hence an isomorphism, weight by weight. This gives the claimed weightwise Nakayama statement.

For a dot-dominant integral target $
u$, including singular, the same truncated projective construction over the target component replaces the labels $W$ by the distinct cosets $W/W_
u$, with the stabilizer computed from the singular facet; the construction proceeds by the same downward orbit induction, and the resulting lifts lie in $\mathcal D_R^{[
u]}(\lambda)$ by construction. No claim is made about central components other than the selected ones.
